summary: Independent line-by-line review of 97f3229..f3f37df confirms the stateless contractor-turn contract and execution path match the specification: typed frozen ContractorTurnContext on BasePlatformAdapter with fail-closed invariants, dispatch ahead of all session bookkeeping, fresh non-cloned persistence-isolated AIAgent per turn, normalized success/ContractorTurnRejected failure result, and deterministic finally-based cleanup on success, error, cancellation, and cleanup-failure paths (non-masking probe-verified with a raising agent.close()). Authentic RED evidence predates both production commits; GREEN reproduced independently on the exact head (24 passed, exit 0). The broad gateway suite's 8 failures reproduce identically on immutable base (recorded full suites: 8 failed on both, same node IDs and error classes; independent isolated re-runs: same 2 fail / 6 pass on both commits) and are demonstrably outside the new behavior. Scope is exactly the three allowed files; recovery preserves parent 33GOD-50 history with a 33GOD-51 Plane reference; head is not merged. Two minor non-blocking findings: cleanup failures inside the shared best-effort _cleanup_agent_resources are swallowed without logging, and the result-normalization rejection branch lacks a dedicated focused test (both verified live by independent probe).

Primary result 'PRIMARY_RESULT' was still returned and the _contractor_agents registry was left empty — a cleanup failure deterministically cleans transient state and cannot replace the primary execution result; the RuntimeError was swallowed silently by the shared best-effort _cleanup_agent_resources (recorded as a minor observability finding).

findings.description: Cleanup failures inside the shared best-effort _cleanup_agent_resources are swallowed with bare 'except Exception: pass' blocks (12417-12418, 12425-12426, 12434-12435) and no logging, so a failing agent.close() leaves no observable trace. The AC-2 non-replacement guarantee is structurally satisfied and probe-verified (raising close() still returned the primary result and emptied the contractor agent registry), and this helper is pre-existing shared infrastructure outside the diff, so the observability nuance does not block spec compliance — but the letter of 'cleanup failures remain observable' is only partially honored.
findings.required_fix: Non-blocking hardening for the downstream quality/security gate or a follow-up: emit a WARNING log when a contractor-turn cleanup step fails (e.g. wrap the _cleanup_agent_resources call site in _run_contractor_agent_sync's finally with a logged boundary), without changing the shared helper's behavior for ordinary sessions.

findings.description: The result-normalization rejection branch (result not a dict / failed is True / completed is not True → ContractorTurnRejected at 21322-21327) has no dedicated focused test in tests/gateway/test_contractor_turns.py, and no focused test injects a cleanup failure to pin non-masking behavior. Both branches were exercised successfully by independent live probes during this review, and every AC-3 coverage area is otherwise represented in the 24-test focused suite, so this is a coverage-resilience gap rather than missing behavior.
findings.required_fix: In a future hardening pass (not this gate), add focused tests pinning (a) the failed=True/completed!=True normalization rejection and (b) a raising agent.close() not masking the turn result, so these probes are captured in the committed suite.
